title: Property Inquiry Status Timeline Ranges
prompt: A real estate listing platform tracks property inquiries through two separate tables: one for inquiries in 'contacted' status and one for inquiries in 'responded' status. Each inquiry is identified by `inquiry_id`. Write a query that collapses consecutive status events into periods, showing one row per consecutive status run per inquiry. Two events are considered consecutive if they appear in adjacent positions when all events for that inquiry are sorted by date, even if calendar days are missing between them. Output columns: `inquiry_id`, `status`, `period_start`, `period_end`. Order the results by `period_start` ascending.
schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE contacted_inquiries (inquiry_id INTEGER NOT NULL, contact_date VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL); CREATE TABLE responded_inquiries (inquiry_id INTEGER NOT NULL, response_date VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL);

composite_moves: UNION ALL the two source tables, each tagged with its status label and casting date from text
ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY inquiry_id ORDER BY event_date) - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY inquiry_id, status ORDER BY event_date) to identify consecutive runs
GROUP BY inquiry_id, status, grp and take MIN(event_date) as period_start, MAX(event_date) as period_end

hints: Consider combining both tables into a single timeline per inquiry, tagged by status.
Use the row-number difference technique separately for each inquiry's timeline to identify consecutive runs of the same status.
Group by inquiry, status, and the consecutive-run identifier, then take the min and max date of each group.
answer_key:
WITH union_events AS (
  SELECT inquiry_id, 'contacted' AS status, contact_date::date AS event_date
  FROM contacted_inquiries
  UNION ALL
  SELECT inquiry_id, 'responded' AS status, response_date::date AS event_date
  FROM responded_inquiries
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT
    inquiry_id,
    status,
    event_date,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY inquiry_id ORDER BY event_date) -
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY inquiry_id, status ORDER BY event_date) AS grp
  FROM union_events
)
SELECT
  inquiry_id,
  status,
  MIN(event_date)::text AS period_start,
  MAX(event_date)::text AS period_end
FROM ranked
GROUP BY inquiry_id, status, grp
ORDER BY period_start;

_meta.scenario: a real estate listing platform tracking saved searches and inquiry rates
